data.title: Standardize deterministic cart development hooks
data.description: Complete one-commit review of protected bounded Lua dev hooks across core, CLI, RPC, playtest, replay/reset, Radiant migration, docs, ECS-watch integration, and rebuilt WASM engine. Combined just check and native/WASM smokes pass.

data.body: INFO: invoke_dev_hook halts the session on ANY error from invoke_validated, including argument-encoding failures in to_lua (non-finite number, oversized string/table, bad key) that occur BEFORE the cart callback runs. The comment justifies halting because 'a callback may have mutated state', which is true for the call/from_lua paths but not for the args-to_lua path — there the session is halted despite nothing having executed. This mirrors phase/name errors (explicitly treated as non-halting host-request errors just above), so it's a slight inconsistency in the public core API. In practice it's unreachable from the agent because rpc/playtest/oneshot pre-validate args via json_to_dev_value with identical budget constants, but a direct core embedder can spuriously and permanently halt a valid deterministic session with a pure bad-input error. Consider converting args before the halt boundary (e.g. validate/encode args, returning a non-halting error, then only halt around the callback + result decode). Non-blocking.

data.reason: Solid, well-bounded implementation. Host closures retained in registry survive global replacement; registration locks after _init; deterministic BTreeMap objects + dense-array detection handle Lua's nondeterministic pairs() order; replay_log correctly interleaves hooks and steps for save/load determinism; identical budget constants across json_to_dev_value and to_lua. clippy clean, core+agent devhooks tests pass. One non-blocking INFO on core args-error halt boundary.

data.body: Confirmed. All agent-facing paths reject the bounded JSON value before Console invocation, so no cart callback or halt occurs there. I am retaining the conservative core halt boundary for this patch because mlua encoding, callback execution, and result decoding currently share one error type; splitting pre-callback errors cleanly deserves a typed invocation-result refactor rather than message matching.

data.reason: Acknowledged as a non-blocking direct-embedder refinement; agent-facing behavior is already non-halting and bounded.
